svg.title: Clean up only when you are done practicing — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Clean up only when you are done practicing
Your Windows host · Notepad lab notes
External practice user
Firewall / private lab boundary
RHEL 9 DMZ application server
NGINX · TLS ends here
Hosted practice application
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
No practice CA trust or lab hosts entry remains in your everyday profile/PC after final cleanup;
unused VMs are powered off.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. If continuing practice, keep the lab isolated and retain the required recovery files under your plan.
2. If finished, close the practice Firefox window. In your original profile’s about:profiles page,
confirm the original is active and remove only SONIC TLS Practice; this removes its practice trust
store.
3. Open the Windows hosts file in administrator Notepad and remove only the 10.90.0.10 app.example.mil
lab line. Do not restore an old complete hosts backup over unrelated later changes.
4. At each VM console run sudo shutdown -h now. Retain or delete only these new practice VMs according
to your learning plan; do not remove existing academy lab servers.
5. The CA is for disposable practice only. Do not export its private keys, add its root to business
systems, or imply that a .mil example is a real authorization.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
